first.rationale:
The loudest signal this week is the competitor's entry pricing, and memory_73 says promotional pricing works for price-sensitive SMB. But memory_73 carries an explicit defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so the reported acquisition/revenue lift may be an artifact of the pooling rather than a real effect. Discounting is also the direction with the worst downside profile against the stated objective — it can buy acquisition numbers while degrading revenue quality, anchoring price expectations, and attracting churn-prone accounts. I do not want to spend the only slot of the week chasing a competitor into a margin war on the strength of a flagged record, so memory_73 is my first verification pull; if the archive shows the lift survives cohort separation, promotional pricing becomes a live option next cycle.

Meanwhile two of the three problems are internal and measurable: activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4%. Onboarding is upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly moves both, whereas activation messaging (memory_91) treats the later symptom only. memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup field reduction lifted SMB activation) point the same way from two independent tests, which is more corroboration than any single direction has. I am pulling memory_86 as the second verification because it is the record I intend to act on and it deserves the same scrutiny I applied to memory_73 — I should check the original experiment before betting the slot on it, not just because it is convenient.

Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries of archived records, and consolidation can strip conditions that mattered. memory_86 was measured on self-serve accounts, so it may not generalize; the current declines may also stem from a mix shift or seasonality that no onboarding change will touch. Simplification carries its own downstream risk — cutting signup fields or onboarding steps can reduce qualification data and route weaker-fit accounts into the funnel, which shows up as a healthy activation number and unhealthy revenue later. I will therefore instrument this as a standard experiment measuring downstream qualified revenue and retention, not just completion and activation rates, and treat the memory_31/memory_86 lifts as provisional until this cohort's own downstream numbers land.
